screen_document.description: Vertical position of the 35 micro-markers encodes log10 of the magnitude and is truthful. The particle relief is a generated Gaussian field whose peaks SUM where entities are close together, so surface height is not a value and does not preserve rank order. Particle colour is a height ramp and is not a category. Depth position is not a value. Marker size restates vertical position. Fog, grain, stars, glow and auto-orbit are decorative. Nothing in the scene is geographic.
screen_document.title: Particle relief over a ranked field
screen_document.useWhen: overview; magnitude; atmosphere
avoid: The claim is about who is highest, or by how much
the axes would be read as places, maps or terrain
any entity must be individually identified
peaks would be counted, compared or measured
values must be read off the scene
screen_document.caveats: This layout's own callout is false as rendered. It asserts 'HIGHEST PEAK · 59.5M · Drake forms the dominant terrain summit', but the surface is a sum of overlapping Gaussian bumps and the largest entity's peak is only the 9th highest of 35 — the tallest surface point belongs to an entity with under a third of the maximum value. Rank correlation between value and rendered peak height is roughly 0.74, not 1.0. Separately, the depth axis labelled 'ERA DEPTH' is a sine wave of the array index with no data behind it, and this was never disclosed to the project owner. The 35 micro-markers ARE positioned truthfully; only the surface and the depth axis are not.

Marker size is a compressive restatement of vertical position and is then cancelled by perspective, so apparent size is not a value. Marker width follows the source image's aspect ratio and is not a value. Marker tilt, colour, fog and exposure are decorative. The dashed benchmark line and the vertical beam are correctly placed from data; the number printed beside them is a fixed authored string and is not computed.

spatial.description: Node height and the length of the stem beneath it encode log10 of the magnitude and are readable. Radius encodes rank in evenly spaced steps and is not magnitude. Angular position is not a value. Node colour encodes the entity's value tier and matches the legend. Node size restates height. The disc, the three concentric rings, the 72 instrument ticks and the five echo points around each node are decorative and are not concentric with the data. Additive blending means overlapping nodes look brighter, and brightness is not a value.
spatial.title: Radial instrument stage with light-node magnitudes
avoid: Angular position or clock position would be read as meaning
the story is the size of a gap rather than an ordering
several entities must be individually identified on screen
any entity has a zero, negative or missing value
a benchmark line or a two-way comparison is needed
spatial.caveats: Radius is rank, not value: the step from the smallest entity to the second smallest is exactly the same distance as the step from the runner-up to the leader. Stem length is proportional to the log difference from the smallest entity in the set, so the shipped 959× value spread renders as a 23.5× stem-length spread. The decorative rings and ticks are centred on the world origin while the data spiral is centred about 0.5–0.6 world units away, so a node's apparent ring membership is off. Unlike the Terrain Cloud layout, this layout's shipped callout is accurate for the shipped data — the largest entity does occupy the highest node.

The disc, the three concentric rings, the 72 instrument ticks and the five echo points around each node are decorative and are not concentric with the data. Additive blending means overlapping nodes look brighter, and brightness is not a value.

spatial.description: Two portrait subjects set side by side on a photographic stage, with a three-line heading, five comparison rows, two kickers, two footers and one note. Every text slot accepts any supplied content, numbers included. Left/right position and portrait size are authored constants and do not encode magnitude, so the frame compares two subjects without ranking them on a scale.
spatial.title: Two-portrait qualitative comparison on a photographic stage
caveats: The 180 generated observations it loads are not rendered (showParticles is false), so nothing appears as a plotted point. Text and portraits are what the frame shows.
As shipped it hardcodes a specific real person's name, two of their photographs and eight lines of copy. None of that is a variable slot until replacements are supplied.
Its name says 'Red Stage' but the surrounding world was changed to pure black at the owner's request; the red comes only from the supplied photograph.

The five comparison rows ship filled with adjective pairs and the scene prints 'CONCEPT COPY - REPLACE WITH VERIFIED STORY DATA' beneath them. That is placeholder content, not a limit on what the rows can hold.
spatial.encoding: Two portrait slots, one background plate and eleven text slots. The five comparison rows are text and take whatever is supplied, including quantities. Position, portrait height and portrait size are authored constants and carry no magnitude; there are no axes or ticks, so any quantity reads from its label rather than from where it sits in the frame.
